title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and improve cache parallelism hygiene
author: Ethan Brooks
description:
Motivation: Over the last year our GitHub Actions surfaced a lot of duplication across lint, test, and release workflows. This PR consolidates reusable workflow templates, reduces duplication, and improves caching/hash keys to reduce CI flakiness and expensive cache misses. It also includes a small hygiene sweep of pinned action versions and removes deprecated steps.

What this does (summary):
- Introduces .github/workflows/ci.yml as a thin orchestrator that delegates to reusable workflows for lint, test, and release.
- Consolidates common steps (checkout, setup-node, artifact/cache helpers) into .github/workflows/reusable/ci-common.yml.
- Improves npm/yarn cache keys to include node-version + lockfile-hash + package-manager to reduce wrong-cache hits.
- Adds an explicit "cache-parallelism" knob and best-practice defaults to our cache helper script (scripts/ci/cache-utils.sh) to avoid thundering-cache restores on big runners.
- Splits lint into fast precommit checks and slower rule-enforcement jobs so PR feedback is faster.
- Pins frequently-changing actions to caret ranges where safe and bumps others to maintained major versions.
- Removes an obsolete release step that published to an internal staging S3 bucket (moved to release automation service).

Checklist:
- [x] Rewrite workflows to use reusable templates
- [x] Add/modify cache keys (node-version + lockfile hash)
- [x] Pin/upgrade GH actions where necessary
- [x] Add unit tests for cache-utils.sh behavior where feasible
- [x] Run CI across representative repositories (redwood, redwood-docs, redwood-sdk-python)

Testing performed:
- Ran workflows on this branch with representative matrix (node 18/20, linux/macos) and measured cache hit rates. Initial run: cache miss rate ~65% due to overly-broad keys. After changes: miss rate down to ~18% for repeated runs.
- Verified lint split: quick checks report in <2m on typical PRs.
- Verified release workflow remains backward compatible when invoked manually (no publish executed in this branch).
- Manually exercised reusable workflow locally via act (limited) and validated step inputs/outputs.

Notable changes to review:
- scripts/ci/cache-utils.sh: added logic to derive cache-key and a parallelism parameter to avoid excessive concurrent restores on runners with low network throughput. Unit tested with mocked env.
- .github/workflows/reusable/ci-common.yml: consolidates setup steps and exposes inputs for package-manager/node-version/cache-key.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: top-level orchestrator that wires lint/test/release flows for PRs and monthly scheduled runs.

CI history:
- First CI run on branch (2026-02-21): lint job failed due to new eslint rule (no-unsafe-negation) in a vendor file. Hotfix committed to exclude generated/vendor from that rule (small override in .eslintrc).
- Second run (2026-02-22): all checks passed except flaky integration test on macos-latest runner (timeout). We bumped the timeout and re-ran.
- Final run (2026-02-24): all checks passed.

Rollout plan:
- Merge as squash to main.
- Monitor CI cache hit metrics on the next 48 hours (dashboard: https://console.internal.redwood/ci/cache-metrics).
- If any repo regresses, revert the workflow file only (ci.yml) while we investigate.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Reusable workflows change semantics for downstream repos. Mitigation: inputs kept explicit and documented; tested across 3 representative repos before merge.
- Risk: Cache key change could increase cold-starts for a single-run, but reduces long-term misses. Mitigation: keys are additive (node+lockfile+pm) and fallback logic exists in cache-utils.sh.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-3720: add observability alerts for unusual cache miss spikes.
- ENG-3751: investigate cross-repo reusable workflow adoption and a small migration guide for SDK repos.

References:
- Linear tickets: ENG-3421, ENG-3580
- Internal doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/ci/reusable-workflows-guidelines

Lucas Rivera: The cache key looks good, but please add node-version explicitly to matrix to avoid accidental mismatch. — replied: Included node-version strat in ci.yml matrix and tests
Samira Khan: Suggest asserting cache-utils.sh behavior in CI smoke job to detect regressions. — replied: Added a lightweight shellcheck + unit invocation in CI-common; heavy tests remain local
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows into reusable templates; improved caching keys and reduced CI flakiness. No user-facing changes.
